BiblicalUsage: Belshazzar was astonied, greatly troubled, his countenance changed, and his lords with him. The Aramaic word is to be perplexed, entangled, unable to make sense of what is happening, and it fits a king staring at writing on his own wall.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe perplexity is the beginning of judgment for the proud, for Belshazzar could not read the writing while Daniel could, and I hold that God still troubles the confident until they listen.
